summary: Penobscot County, ME site where the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a tower as gone; no citable source read gives its build date, move or current state.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source read describes the site now or whether the summit is open to visitors

evidence.supports: Rollins Mountain is in Penobscot County; FFLA lists its tower as gone

notes_for_editor: Only one citable source. The FFLA Maine chapter state listing table (last update 12/30/2021; page URL not identified, so not cited) gives Rollins Mt., Lincoln, Penobscot, elevation 940 ft, a 60 ft tower installed 1950, and says it was moved to the center of Canaan in 1977 as an exhibit and removed from Canaan sometime after 1989. A Maine chapter Facebook post (https://www.facebook.com/forest-fire-lookout-association-maine-chapter-103171429203527/photos/117356674451669/) says the tower was moved to Canaan and then disappeared, but the page returned no readable text, so none of it is quoted or footnoted. The Sun Journal table does not list Rollins. The story is well under the 120-word floor because nothing citable beyond the county listing could be read. Adding the chapter table, or a readable copy of the post, would allow the build and fate to be told; Canaan is in Somerset County, which the brief does not mention.
